title: Google Cloud Examples
description: Small Google Cloud Platform examples from the lessons. Each example links back to its explanation and practice task.

examples.title: Meet Google Cloud
examples.description: Google Cloud provides hosted services for computing, storage and data work. Begin by matching a service to a small, clear need.
examples.code:
Need: store the files for a club page
Data: index.html, styles.css and logo.png
No need: visitor passwords or a custom database

examples.title: Projects organise resources
examples.description: A Google Cloud project groups resources and settings. It has a project name, a project ID and a project number with different roles.
examples.code:
Display name: Club practice
Project ID: fictional-club-practice
Project number: assigned by the service

examples.title: Regions and zones
examples.description: A region is a geographic area. A zone is a deployment area within a region. Some resources are zonal, regional or global.
examples.code:
Region example: us-central1
Zone example: us-central1-a
Plan: check the location type of each service

examples.title: IAM roles and principals
examples.description: A principal is an identity asking for access. An IAM role groups permissions, and a policy binds a role to principals at a resource scope.
examples.code:
Principal: fictional reviewer
Role: an appropriate read-only role
Scope: the intended practice resource

examples.title: Service accounts are workload identities
examples.description: A service account represents an application or workload. It is different from a person's user account.
examples.code:
Workload: approved report task
Identity: its own service account
Access: only the data needed for the report

examples.title: Cloud Storage objects
examples.description: Cloud Storage keeps objects in buckets. An object name identifies the object within its bucket.
examples.code:
Bucket: fictional-club-files
Object name: images/logo.png
Data: the logo file

examples.title: Object versions and lifecycle rules
examples.description: Versioning and lifecycle rules can help retain or clean up object versions. They need a deliberate policy so useful data is not lost or kept forever.
examples.code:
Keep current page files
Retain older versions for an agreed recovery period
Review lifecycle cleanup rules before enabling them

examples.title: Compute Engine virtual machines
examples.description: Compute Engine provides virtual machines. You choose a machine configuration, image and location and manage the guest software.
examples.code:
Planned VM: one small learning instance
Image: a supported operating system
Owner work: patching, access and monitoring

examples.title: VPC networks and subnets
examples.description: Google Cloud VPC networks are global resources. Their subnets are regional. This is a useful distinction from some other cloud network models.
examples.code:
VPC: club-network
Subnet: club-subnet in us-central1
Address range: 10.3.1.0/24

examples.title: Firewall rules control connections
examples.description: VPC firewall rules allow or deny selected traffic for targeted resources. A good rule names the needed sources, protocol and ports.
examples.code:
Target: intended practice web VM
Allowed: HTTPS on TCP 443 from approved sources
Administration: restricted separately

examples.title: Logging and Monitoring
examples.description: Cloud Logging records supported events. Cloud Monitoring tracks metrics and alert conditions. Use both to understand a problem.
examples.code:
Metric: failed requests per minute
Log event: one request could not find a file
Action: check the file path and deployment contents

examples.title: Budgets and labels
examples.description: Budgets help monitor spend and send notifications. Labels help group costs by project purpose. Neither is a reason to skip cost review.
examples.code:
Label: purpose=learning
Fictional monthly budget: 6 units
Alert at half: 3 units
